messages:
Maya R: Heads up — noticed a small but consistent uptick in function-call / structured-output failures from the fp8-2026-02 build when running sampling workloads (temp 0.6-0.9). Errors are JSON parse failures from downstream toolchain.

Maya R: Quick numbers from last 6h: 0.3% -> 1.2% invalid JSON emits on /generate-toolargs route for model fp8-2026-02, baseline int8-gptq is ~0.4%. Pattern spikes on bursty traffic.

Devin K: Can you paste a minimal repro and the exact sampling config?

Maya R: repro below (this is one of the failing outputs):
```
PROMPT:
{
  "task": "format_args",
  "schema": {"cmd":"string","args":"list"},
  "input":"list files in /tmp"
}
CONFIG: temperature=0.75, top_p=0.95, max_tokens=128, streaming=false

MODEL OUTPUT (truncated / invalid):
{
  "cmd": "ls",
  "args": ["-la", "/tmp"]
  }

(note missing closing bracket for outer json occasionally, or stray control tokens)
```

Samir P: Interesting — looks like tokenization boundary or early stopping during sampling. fp8 path may produce slightly different tokenization probabilities so sampling can emit a partial close brace then stop. Did we see the same with deterministic decoding?

Maya R: deterministic (temp=0 top_p=1, greedy) seems fine for same prompt. Problem reproduces quickly when enabling nucleus/t sampling. Also observed higher incidence when sequence length hits ~110-120 (near max_tokens).

Rachel L: Could be combined effect: quantized logits perturbation + sampling tail risk + KV cache cutoff when we reach per-request token budget. Suggest two quick experiments: 1) run the same prompt with forced eos penalty/clamping; 2) compare token-level logit diffs between fp8 and int8 for the same seed.

Devin K: Can you run this quick curl to collect logits and tokens for 50 runs on fp8 and int8?
```bash
for i in {1..50}; do \
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.test/v1/generate -d '{"model":"fp8-2026-02","prompt":"<..>","sampling":{...},"logprobs":5}' 
>> fp8-samples.json; done
```

Maya R: starting a short job now (kicking off 50 runs into /tmp/fp8-samples.json). Will attach summary when done.

eval-bot: quick-run report ready: fp8-2026-02 50 samples -> 7 invalid JSON (14%), int8-gptq-2026-02 50 samples -> 1 invalid JSON (2%). Median length fp8=118 tokens, int8=115 tokens.

Samir P: 14% in the quick-run is higher than prod numbers, but sampling seed randomness can blow up. Can you include the raw token sequences for the failing ones? I want to see whether the decoder produced an EOF or a special token mid-brace.

Maya R: attached snippets (added to thread): failing examples show pattern: '... \"args\": ["-la", "/tmp"]\n }' vs '... \"args\": ["-la", "/tmp"]\n' (missing final newline+brace). Some cases have a token split like '\\u012' in between.

Rachel L: Token split hints at tokenizer sub-tokenization of braces? But braces are normal ascii. Could be internal post-processing step that strips trailing bytes when quant error yields control-like bytes. Check the post-server sanitization/UTF-8 handling.

Devin K: Ops — any infra/log indications?

ops-bot: alert: increased /generate-toolargs 400s from cluster-a (fp8 pool) between 13:04-13:27 UTC, scaled from 120 -> 160 instances. Error logs: JSONDecodeError in parser (byte 127).

Samir P: Byte 127 — non-printable. That aligns with some quant noise mapping to high ascii when we do faster int8->fp8 kernel path. I'll run the model in CPU float playback to diff logits around the failing tokens.

Maya R: Plan: Samir to run token-level logit diff (fp8 vs int8) + ray job to replay 1k seeded samples; Rachel to add a temporary output sanitizer (strip non-printable, ensure closing braces) in agent pipeline for the canary; Devin to run a controlled A/B test with reduced top_p for 24h. I'll open a short PR for sanitizer.

Samir P: Started a debug job: /jobs/debug/2005554321-logit-diff (will upload artifacts). Initial 200 samples show fp8 higher tail variance around 0.6-0.9 probability events causing early eos in ~11 cases.

Rachel L: I'll prototype sanitizer by tomorrow morning — simple: trim trailing non-utf8, run json.loads and if fails try to append closing brace heuristics and re-parse, but log all corrections so we can measure delta. Not ideal but buys time.

Maya R: If sanitizer changes output shape for downstream tools, we should tag as sanitized and send to a 'retry' queue rather than silently mutate. Also add telemetry to count sanitized vs raw.

Devin K: Agreed. I'll set up a canary route: fp8-sampled-sanitized (10% traffic) vs fp8-sampled-raw (90%) and we can measure user-visible errors.

eval-bot: scheduled 1k-sample bakeoff for fp8 vs int8 with sampling=0.75 top_p=0.95, job id bakeoff-2005554321-1k queued. ETA ~3h.

Maya R: Thanks everyone. Samir — please ping when you have the logit diff artifact. We'll reconvene if sanitizer reduces runtime errors. :thumbsup:

Samir P: will do. starting deeper bisect of kernel flags (fp8-kernel-v2 vs v1) after logit diff.

Rachel L: FYI also saw a small TODO: run same test with AWQ quant path (we haven't validated AWQ for this model family under sampling). Adding to backlog.

Maya R: ok adding AWQ check as follow-up. If anyone hits a reproducer please post minimal prompt+output.

Devin K: thx — dropping quick link to repro script: https://phabricator.redwood/s/ML/struct-repro/blob/main/run_repro.sh

Maya R: closing loop for now — will update thread with artifacts (fp8-samples.json, sanitizer PR link, bakeoff results).
